After touring for *How to Be a Human Being*, the band released two singles; "Tokyo Drifting", a duet with [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry"), on 14 November 2019,[[2]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-tokyodriftingrepublicrecords-2) and "Your Love (Déjà Vu)" on 19 February 2020.[[15]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-15) On 1 May 2020, the band released a single named "Dreamland", and announced an [album of the same name](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album) "Dreamland (Glass Animals album)") to be released on 10 July 2020.[[16]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-16) The beginnings of Dreamland originated after drummer Joe Seaward's bike accident in Dublin. While spending long hours by Seaward's side in the hospital as he recovered, Bayley started "writing down memories and searching for more memories." Those memories eventually evolved into the nostalgic and very personal *Dreamland* album full of references to Bayley's childhood and other points in his life.[[5]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:1-5)

On 28 June, the band announced that the album had been delayed, to "keep focus on the [Black Lives Matter](Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement and the [discussions taking place around racism](2020_United_States_racial_injustice_reckoning "2020 United States racial injustice reckoning") and [police brutality](Police_brutality "Police brutality") around the world."[[17]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-17) In the lead-up to *Dreamland*, Glass Animals launched an open-source website where fans could access and download song samples, artwork, and other content related to the album.[[5]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:1-5) *Dreamland* was released on 7 August 2020 via Polydor Records. In an interview with *Atwood Magazine*, Bayley explained: "I guess the goal with this record was to make something that was incredibly honest and incredibly us."[[18]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-18) The album entered the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") at number two. "[Heat Waves](Heat_Waves "Heat Waves")" was included on the *[FIFA 21](FIFA_21 "FIFA 21")* soundtrack.

On 23 January 2021, "Heat Waves" placed first on the [Triple J Hottest 100 of 2020](Triple_J_Hottest_100%2C_2020 "Triple J Hottest 100, 2020") in Australia, with "Tangerine" placing at 18th and "Your Love (Déjà Vu)" at 51st. The following month, "Heat Waves" reached number one on the [ARIA Singles Chart](ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts").[[19]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-AUS-19) In April 2021, "Tokyo Drifting" was featured in a television commercial released by [Peloton](Peloton_(exercise_equipment_company) "Peloton (exercise equipment company)") as part of their Champions Collection campaign.[[20]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-20)

***Dreamland*** is the third studio album by English [indie rock](Indie_rock "Indie rock") band [Glass Animals](Glass_Animals "Glass Animals"). It was released on 7 August 2020, having been pushed back from its initial release date of 10 July 2020.[[1]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Postponement-1)

*Dreamland* is the band's first album since *[How to Be a Human Being](How_to_Be_a_Human_Being "How to Be a Human Being")* (2016) and was conceived in the aftermath of their drummer being involved in a near-fatal collision in July 2018. The album was written and produced almost entirely by frontman [Dave Bayley](Dave_Bayley "Dave Bayley") and features heavily autobiographical lyrics, a radical difference from the band's previous work. It derives musical and lyrical inspiration from Bayley's childhood in Texas, particularly from the popular culture and media of 1990s and early 2000s America. The album has been described as being "drenched in" nostalgia[[2]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Independent-2) and is structured around a series of interludes of audio from Bayley's childhood home videos. *Dreamland* was influenced by the [R&B](Contemporary_R%26B "Contemporary R&B") and [hip hop music](Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") from the early 2000s, and features an appearance from American rapper [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry").

*Dreamland* received mostly favourable reviews from music critics and debuted at number 2 on the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") and number 7 on the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). Five singles were issued in promotion of the album: "Tokyo Drifting" (with [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry")), "Your Love (Déjà Vu)", the eponymously named "Dreamland", the chart-topping "[Heat Waves](Heat_Waves "Heat Waves")", and "It's All So Incredibly Loud". A [visual album](Visual_album "Visual album"), entitled *Dreamland: The Home Movies*, was released on <VHS> shortly after the album's release.

## Background and recording

**St Edward's School** is a [public school](Public_school_(United_Kingdom) "Public school (United Kingdom)") (English [fee-charging](Private_schools_in_the_United_Kingdom "Private schools in the United Kingdom") [boarding](Boarding_school "Boarding school") and [day school](Day_school "Day school")) in <Oxford>, England. Termly fees in 2023/2024 are £15,660 for boarding and £12,528 for day pupils.[[2]](St_Edward's_School%2C_Oxford#cite_note-2) The school is also affiliated to the [Church of England](Church_of_England "Church of England").

The school teaches the <GCSE>, [A Level](Advanced_Level_(UK) "Advanced Level (UK)") and International Baccalaureate (IB) qualifications. The sixth form is split evenly between pupils studying A Levels and the IB Diploma.

## History

The school was founded in 1863 by Thomas Chamberlain, student of [Christ Church, Oxford](Christ_Church%2C_Oxford "Christ Church, Oxford") and vicar of [St Thomas the Martyr's Church, Oxford](St_Thomas_the_Martyr's_Church%2C_Oxford "St Thomas the Martyr's Church, Oxford"). The original school building was Mackworth Hall, which then stood on New Inn Hall Street in central Oxford.

In 1873, after a storm damaged the school buildings and in anticipation of growing numbers, A. B. Simeon, the first Warden, moved the school to [Summertown](Summertown%2C_Oxford "Summertown, Oxford"). At the time, the site was on the boundary of Oxford and surrounded by farmland, and Simeon bought a large plot for the school. The school remains on the 100-acre (0.40 km2) site today, with the [Quadrangle](Quadrangle_(architecture) "Quadrangle (architecture)") and playing fields on opposite sides of [Woodstock Road](Woodstock_Road_(Oxford) "Woodstock Road (Oxford)").

Simeon created an [independent school](Independent_school "Independent school") with monastic-style buildings around a quadrangle.[[3]](St_Edward's_School%2C_Oxford#cite_note-3) The original buildings were designed by [William Wilkinson](William_Wilkinson_(architect) "William Wilkinson (architect)"). The north range was built in 1873 and 1886, the [gatehouse](Gatehouse "Gatehouse") in 1879, and the east range, including Big School and the library, in 1881. Wilkinson's most significant building at St Edward's is the chapel, built in 1876.[[4]](St_Edward's_School%2C_Oxford#cite_note-4)

Henry Ewing Kendall was warden from 1925 to 1954.[[5]](St_Edward's_School%2C_Oxford#cite_note-5)

***Dreamland*** is the third studio album by English [indie rock](Indie_rock "Indie rock") band [Glass Animals](Glass_Animals "Glass Animals"). It was released on 7 August 2020, having been pushed back from its initial release date of 10 July 2020.[[1]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Postponement-1)

*Dreamland* is the band's first album since *[How to Be a Human Being](How_to_Be_a_Human_Being "How to Be a Human Being")* (2016) and was conceived in the aftermath of their drummer being involved in a near-fatal collision in July 2018. The album was written and produced almost entirely by frontman [Dave Bayley](Dave_Bayley "Dave Bayley") and features heavily autobiographical lyrics, a radical difference from the band's previous work. It derives musical and lyrical inspiration from Bayley's childhood in Texas, particularly from the popular culture and media of 1990s and early 2000s America. The album has been described as being "drenched in" nostalgia[[2]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Independent-2) and is structured around a series of interludes of audio from Bayley's childhood home videos. *Dreamland* was influenced by the [R&B](Contemporary_R%26B "Contemporary R&B") and [hip hop music](Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") from the early 2000s, and features an appearance from American rapper [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry").

*Dreamland* received mostly favourable reviews from music critics and debuted at number 2 on the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") and number 7 on the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). Five singles were issued in promotion of the album: "Tokyo Drifting" (with [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry")), "Your Love (Déjà Vu)", the eponymously named "Dreamland", the chart-topping "[Heat Waves](Heat_Waves "Heat Waves")", and "It's All So Incredibly Loud". A [visual album](Visual_album "Visual album"), entitled *Dreamland: The Home Movies*, was released on <VHS> shortly after the album's release.

## Background and recording

On 2 July 2018, Glass Animals drummer Joe Seaward was hit by a [lorry](Truck "Truck") while cycling in <Dublin>, <Ireland> and suffered a broken leg and fractured skull, and subsequently underwent brain surgery.[[3]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-3) The band cancelled their remaining tour dates for rest of the year as a result.[[4]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-4) With Seaward's fate unknown at the time, [Dave Bayley](Dave_Bayley "Dave Bayley") said it was "difficult to look forwards" and he found himself looking backwards, thinking back to old memories and "finding comfort in them even if they were uncomfortable in themselves".[[5]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-UDM-5) In September 2018, Seaward posted an update detailing his recovery in having to learn to talk, read, and walk again, and revealed he started playing the drums again.[[6]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-6)[[7]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-7)

Dave Bayley (left) and Joe Seaward (right) of [Glass Animals](Glass_Animals "Glass Animals")

While Seaward was in recovery, Bayley travelled repeatedly to [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"). Bayley** (March 26, 1933 – May 10, 2020) was an American political scientist who taught at the [University of Denver](University_of_Denver "University of Denver") and the [State University of New York at Albany](State_University_of_New_York_at_Albany "State University of New York at Albany").[[1]](David_H._Bayley#cite_note-mcpeekobit-1) He was dean of SUNY Albany's School of Criminal Justice from 1995-2004 and was Distinguished Professor Emeritus.[[2]](David_H._Bayley#cite_note-albany.edu-2) He authored 18 books,[[1]](David_H._Bayley#cite_note-mcpeekobit-1) and he became a "policing research pioneer."[[3]](David_H._Bayley#cite_note-heslopcontribution-3) Bayley was described in 2015 as “America’s principal, most respected and longest serving policing expert at-large and the world’s preeminent scholar of international policing studies.”[[2]](David_H._Bayley#cite_note-albany.edu-2)

### 2016–2019: *How to Be a Human Being*

On 16 May 2016, the band released the lead single, "Life Itself", from their second album *[How to Be a Human Being](How_to_Be_a_Human_Being "How to Be a Human Being")*.[[11]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-11) "Life Itself" peaked at number 14 on *Billboard*'s Alternative Songs chart and spent 26 weeks on Sirius XM's Alt-18 chart, peaking at number one.[[12]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:0-12) A music video for the song was released on 7 June 2016. The band also created a website based on the character from "Life Itself".

On 25 July, a second single from the album, "Youth", was released along with its music video.[[12]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:0-12) This song was also used as a soundtrack in the popular football video game by [EA Sports](EA_Sports "EA Sports"), *[FIFA 17](FIFA_17 "FIFA 17")*. Four days before the release of the album, on 22 August, the band released a third single, "Season 2 Episode 3", about a girl who "spends her entire time watching TV, lounging around, not doing anything, being high, eating mayonnaise from a jar".[[13]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-13)

The full album *How to Be a Human Being* was released on 26 August 2016 by Wolf Tone and [Caroline International](Caroline_International "Caroline International") in Europe, and [Harvest Records](Harvest_Records "Harvest Records") in the United States. It was inspired by stories of strangers that Bayley met on tour,[[3]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:2-3) with each song telling a different story from a different perspective.

In July 2018, drummer Joe Seaward was seriously injured when he was hit by a [lorry](Lorry "Lorry") while cycling in <Dublin>. Seaward's accident and recovery resulted in the band cancelling their remaining tour dates for rest of the year.[[14]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-14)

### 2019–present: *Dreamland*

After touring for *How to Be a Human Being*, the band released two singles; "Tokyo Drifting", a duet with [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry"), on 14 November 2019,[[2]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-tokyodriftingrepublicrecords-2) and "Your Love (Déjà Vu)" on 19 February 2020.[[15]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-15) On 1 May 2020, the band released a single named "Dreamland", and announced an [album of the same name](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album) "Dreamland (Glass Animals album)") to be released on 10 July 2020.[[16]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-16) The beginnings of Dreamland originated after drummer Joe Seaward's bike accident in Dublin. While spending long hours by Seaward's side in the hospital as he recovered, Bayley started "writing down memories and searching for more memories." Those memories eventually evolved into the nostalgic and very personal *Dreamland* album full of references to Bayley's childhood and other points in his life.[[5]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:1-5)

On 28 June, the band announced that the album had been delayed, to "keep focus on the [Black Lives Matter](Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement and the [discussions taking place around racism](2020_United_States_racial_injustice_reckoning "2020 United States racial injustice reckoning") and [police brutality](Police_brutality "Police brutality") around the world."[[17]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-17) In the lead-up to *Dreamland*, Glass Animals launched an open-source website where fans could access and download song samples, artwork, and other content related to the album.[[5]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-:1-5) *Dreamland* was released on 7 August 2020 via Polydor Records. In an interview with *Atwood Magazine*, Bayley explained: "I guess the goal with this record was to make something that was incredibly honest and incredibly us."[[18]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-18) The album entered the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") at number two. "[Heat Waves](Heat_Waves "Heat Waves")" was included on the *[FIFA 21](FIFA_21 "FIFA 21")* soundtrack.

On 23 January 2021, "Heat Waves" placed first on the [Triple J Hottest 100 of 2020](Triple_J_Hottest_100%2C_2020 "Triple J Hottest 100, 2020") in Australia, with "Tangerine" placing at 18th and "Your Love (Déjà Vu)" at 51st. The following month, "Heat Waves" reached number one on the [ARIA Singles Chart](ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts").[[19]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-AUS-19) In April 2021, "Tokyo Drifting" was featured in a television commercial released by [Peloton](Peloton_(exercise_equipment_company) "Peloton (exercise equipment company)") as part of their Champions Collection campaign.[[20]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-20)

A bonus track and single, "I Don’t Wanna Talk (I Just Wanna Dance)", was included on the *[FIFA 22](FIFA_22 "FIFA 22")* soundtrack.[[21]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-21) After a record-breaking 59-week climb on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), "Heat Waves" topped the chart for the week ending 12 March 2022.[[22]](Glass_Animals#cite_note-22)

***Dreamland*** is the third studio album by English [indie rock](Indie_rock "Indie rock") band [Glass Animals](Glass_Animals "Glass Animals"). It was released on 7 August 2020, having been pushed back from its initial release date of 10 July 2020.[[1]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Postponement-1)

*Dreamland* is the band's first album since *[How to Be a Human Being](How_to_Be_a_Human_Being "How to Be a Human Being")* (2016) and was conceived in the aftermath of their drummer being involved in a near-fatal collision in July 2018. The album was written and produced almost entirely by frontman [Dave Bayley](Dave_Bayley "Dave Bayley") and features heavily autobiographical lyrics, a radical difference from the band's previous work. It derives musical and lyrical inspiration from Bayley's childhood in Texas, particularly from the popular culture and media of 1990s and early 2000s America. The album has been described as being "drenched in" nostalgia[[2]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Independent-2) and is structured around a series of interludes of audio from Bayley's childhood home videos. *Dreamland* was influenced by the [R&B](Contemporary_R%26B "Contemporary R&B") and [hip hop music](Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") from the early 2000s, and features an appearance from American rapper [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry").

*Dreamland* received mostly favourable reviews from music critics and debuted at number 2 on the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart")

***Dreamland*** is the third studio album by English [indie rock](Indie_rock "Indie rock") band [Glass Animals](Glass_Animals "Glass Animals"). It was released on 7 August 2020, having been pushed back from its initial release date of 10 July 2020.[[1]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Postponement-1)

*Dreamland* is the band's first album since *[How to Be a Human Being](How_to_Be_a_Human_Being "How to Be a Human Being")* (2016) and was conceived in the aftermath of their drummer being involved in a near-fatal collision in July 2018. The album was written and produced almost entirely by frontman [Dave Bayley](Dave_Bayley "Dave Bayley") and features heavily autobiographical lyrics, a radical difference from the band's previous work. It derives musical and lyrical inspiration from Bayley's childhood in Texas, particularly from the popular culture and media of 1990s and early 2000s America. The album has been described as being "drenched in" nostalgia[[2]](Dreamland_(Glass_Animals_album)#cite_note-Independent-2) and is structured around a series of interludes of audio from Bayley's childhood home videos. *Dreamland* was influenced by the [R&B](Contemporary_R%26B "Contemporary R&B") and [hip hop music](Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") from the early 2000s, and features an appearance from American rapper [Denzel Curry](Denzel_Curry "Denzel Curry").

*Dreamland* received mostly favourable reviews from music critics and debuted at number 2 on the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart")
